classification.difficultyReason: Connect parallel markings, vertically opposite angles, parallelogram properties and angles on a straight line.

content.prompt: Determine the value of $a$ in this diagram. Explain your reasoning.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14 diagram in the lower middle of the page
spec.description: Two parallelograms meet at their central vertices between common upper and lower horizontal reference lines. Single arrows mark sides ascending right; double arrows mark sides descending right. Three angle arcs show 71° at the crossing, 28° above the lower line extending left, and a° above the lower line extending right.
spec.mathematics: Each quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides parallel. The central right-facing angle is 71°; its vertically opposite angle is the central interior angle of the left parallelogram. The lower interior angle of that parallelogram lies between the 28° and a° angles on a straight line.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens 71°, 28° and a° are visible. The auxiliary angle x and calculated values are confined to answers.

answer.short: $a=43^\circ$. The lower interior angle is $109^\circ$, so $a=180^\circ-28^\circ-109^\circ$.
answer.worked:
The parallel markings show that both pairs of opposite sides of the left quadrilateral are parallel, so it is a parallelogram. Let $x$ be its lower interior angle. Its central interior angle is $71^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal. Opposite angles in a parallelogram are equal, so its four angles are $x$, $71^\circ$, $x$ and $71^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}2x+71^\circ+71^\circ&=360^\circ&&\text{(angle sum of a quadrilateral)}\\2x&=218^\circ\\x&=109^\circ\\a+28^\circ+109^\circ&=180^\circ&&\text{(angles on a straight line)}\\a&=43^\circ\end{align*}$$
